blurTest.evidence: In both /tmp/namesnap-ipad-picker-final-portrait.png and /tmp/namesnap-ipad-picker-landscape.png, the centered wheel band, contestant input card, segmented mode control, and winner strip retain a clear hierarchy without relying on copy.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The wheel card is visually distinct from the input, winner, history, and pool regions; the full-width selected band is centered and immediately recognizable in portrait and landscape.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The iPad render immediately communicates add contestants, select Wheel, and spin; the selected contestant is centered in the dominant wheel band.

realityTest.evidence: The screenshots use a realistic 18-name classroom or stream pool, numbered rows, a recent winner, no-repeat state, and an actively selectable wheel rather than placeholders.

journeyTest.evidence: The rendered state coherently carries the same contestant data through input, wheel selection, winner output, recent winners, and remaining pool.

platformTest.evidence: Native iPad portrait and landscape simulator renders respect safe areas and the 900-point content measure; an iPhone regression render at /tmp/namesnap-iphone-picker-regression.png preserves the centered native picker.

buyerValueTest.evidence: Teachers and streamers can read the selected name at a distance, operate the wheel from either edge of a large iPad, and see winner history without changing screens.

implementationTest.evidence: The production implementation uses a no-intrinsic-width UIPickerView subclass, an explicit proposed-width sizing contract, full-width SwiftUI framing, and centered reusable row labels.

screenFindings.finding: Contestant labels and the selected band are centered across the full wheel card.
The 900-point content measure stays centered and the wheel remains visually balanced on the wider canvas.
A physical far-right drag changed the picker selection and produced the Katy Perry winner state.
The full-width change keeps the compact-phone wheel centered and legible.

repairs.issue: The iPad picker previously retained UIPickerView's narrow intrinsic width, leaving names and the drag target on the left.
repairs.repair: Removed the picker's intrinsic horizontal size, accepted the full proposed SwiftUI width, centered custom row labels, and made the selected band span the wheel card.

repairs.issue: A drag at the far-left side originally scrolled the parent page instead of spinning the wheel.
repairs.repair: Expanded the actual UIKit picker hit region rather than only centering it inside a wider wrapper; separate left- and right-edge interaction checks now change selection.

verdict: Approved after rendered portrait, landscape, left-edge, right-edge, and iPhone regression inspection. The iPad wheel is centered and genuinely interactive across its width.
